children: Meta Platforms (META) faces a proposed up to $18B settlement over alleged harm to children; this legal risk coincides with its push to develop and roll out AI products like Muse.
Wells Fargo cut Meta Platforms (META) 2026 operating income forecast 12% after flagging an expected $10 billion legal settlement charge in Q3.
Meta guided 2026 capex of $130–$145B, with heavy spending in Q2. Elevated capex cut reported free cash flow as firm builds out large AI infrastructure.
Wells Fargo raised Meta Platforms (META) price target to $796 from $640, citing early signs of a new product cycle around Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse launches; stock jumped ~6.9% intraday.
Meta provided a $28B guarantee for its Hyperion data‑center deal with Blue Owl, backing about $27B of project financing while keeping most of the obligation off Meta’s balance sheet.
Truist projects Meta's Muse product could add up to $28.5B in revenue by 2030, modeling $20 and $100 monthly tiers and positioning Muse as a non-advertising revenue source.
Meta (META) set tiered Muse AI pricing: free 100M tokens/week; $20/mo for 500M/week; $100/mo for 3B/week. Large free/paid quotas may mute near-term revenue while boosting user adoption.
Meta Platforms (META) unveiled Petal, a 7,000 km U.S.–France subsea cable with 1 Pb/s capacity, built with NEC and Sumitomo Electric, landing in France via Orange, due 2029.
Meta Platforms (META): analysts note rising consumer AI agents as a growth driver, $759 target implying ~14% upside; focus on sustaining user engagement and monetizing AI adoption.
Meta Platforms (META) rolled out Muse Spark 1.3 this month, boosting performance on long-running agentic and coding tasks; part of a series of AI model upgrades timed before investor events.
